newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT TO DISCUSS AIR COMPANIES' MERGER.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT TO DISCUSS AIR COMPANIES' MERGER.

text.p: Lithuania's trasport ministry said on Thursday that the merger of two airline companies, Lithuanian Airlines and Air Lietuva, might be considered in the cabinet meeting on next Wednesday.

"The civil aviation department was obliged to draw a draft of the government's decision, it is ready now and I hope it will be approved in the next cabinet meeting," Transport Minister Algis Zhvaliauskas told a news conference.
The ministry decided earlier this month to merge Lithuanian Airlines and smaller Air Lietuva to make them more attractive during the privatisation process.
It is planned that Air Lietuva will be merged as a daughter company of Lithuanian Airlines.
Zhvaliauskas said that the government's position remained firm that at least 51 percent of the company be in Lithuanian hands after the sell-off to preserve its status as national carrier.
The Lithuanian government included the two companies on a list of key infrustructure enterprises slated for privatisation through international bids in 1997-1998.
